description:
1. The agent reads SKILL.md and discovers it must first run `python scripts/extract_relativity_pages.py --input productions/ --recurse --output <some>.json` to extract per-page document IDs and text.
2. The agent inspects the JSON output. Several pages have two Bates numbers in the bottom-right (e.g., 'HLTH 00142  HLTH 00089'). The SKILL.md mandates: 'if two numbers appear, use the smaller one'. So those pages resolve to doc ID 89 (not 142), 178 (not 201), 55 (not 67), and 289 (not 310). A naive agent that picks the first or larger number will produce wrong document IDs.
3. The agent maps each page to the legal theory (upcoding/fraudulent billing), classifying pages as supports/undermines/neutral.
4. The agent drafts deposition questions grouped by document ID. The correct document IDs are 55, 89, 178, and 289 — in ascending numeric order. IDs 67, 142, 201, and 310 must NOT appear as document headings.
5. Under every question the agent must include a 'Reason why we ask this question' section and a 'Quote from the document to use in deposition in case the opponent party denies' section with a verbatim quote (or the specific placeholder if none available).
6. The final `deposition_questions.md` follows the structure in `references/deposition_output_template.md`.
